paper.title_en: Number Theory of Decaying Turbulence 2: The Energy Spectrum and the Riemann Zeta Zeros
paper.abstract_en: The odd Euler ensemble, the locally stable attractor of the momentum-loop dynamics of freely decaying incompressible turbulence, has a self-similar energy spectrum \(E(k,t)=L^{-3/2}H(kL)\), \(L\sim\sqrt{\tildeνt}\), which does not depend on the dimension of space. We compute its scaling function as a Mellin--Barnes integral whose amplitude contains the ratio \(ζ(p+15/2)/ζ(p+17/2)\) of Riemann zeta functions; the odd ensemble differs from the even one by a prime-\(2\) Euler factor. The integral is evaluated by deforming the contour to Lefschetz thimbles. The non-trivial zeros of \(ζ(s)\) generate a vertical wall of complex poles. As \(ξ=\log(k\sqrt{\tildeνt})\) increases, the thimble traps them in a Stokes staircase, first collectively and then a few at a time, and Berry smoothing turns each trapping into an analytic activation of an exponentially small oscillatory term. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis and simplicity of the zeros, all these poles lie on one wall and their activations accumulate only at infinite time: the spectrum is analytic at every finite time and has an essential singularity at \(t=\infty\). The same analysis gives the second-order structure function, whose index falls continuously from \(2\) to \(0\) without an inertial plateau, and the decay laws, energy \(\propto t^{-5/4}\) and enstrophy \(\propto t^{-9/4}\). The operator representation and the stability of the Euler ensemble are derived in the first paper of this series, and the comparison with simulations and experiments is given in the third.
